item.title: Hosting visiting partners in Samarkand
item.context_text: Your company in Tashkent is hosting two partners, Lucía and Marco, from a travel company in Spain. You've organised a one-day trip to Samarkand for Thursday, and you are their guide for the day.
item.objective_text: Check the programme, adapt it when plans change, confirm the new plan in writing, and welcome the guests on site.
item.target_grammar: future forms for arrangements and suggestions (We'll take… How about… I've arranged for…)
item.cultural_note: Visitors to historic mausoleums in Uzbekistan are usually asked to dress modestly. Hosts often mention it in advance so guests are not caught out.
success_conditions: Understand the programme and the dress code
Identify what has changed and the guests' priorities
Send a revised plan that solves the travel and food problems
Welcome the guests at Registan and outline the day

children.title: Read the programme
children.instructions: Read the programme you sent the guests. Then answer the questions.
children.prompt_text:
Thursday programme
08:00 Fast train from Tashkent (arrives 10:10)
10:45 Registan Square, guided visit (90 min)
12:30 Lunch: plov at a family restaurant
14:00 Gur-e-Amir Mausoleum
15:30 Free time at Siab Bazaar
17:30 Dinner meeting with local tour operators
20:30 Train back to Tashkent
Please note: when visiting mausoleums, wear clothes that cover your shoulders and knees.

questions.prompt: How long is the guided visit at Registan?
What should the guests wear for Gur-e-Amir?
options: Clothes that cover shoulders and knees
questions.explanation: "Wear clothes that cover your shoulders and knees."

children.title: Listen to Lucía
children.instructions: On Tuesday, Lucía leaves you a voice message. Listen and answer the questions.
children.prompt_text: Hi, it's Lucía. Quick message about Thursday. Unfortunately our flight to Tashkent has been changed, so we'll only land at seven fifteen that morning, which is far too tight for the eight o'clock train. Is there a later option? We'd really hate to miss Registan, so if something has to go, maybe drop the bazaar. Oh, and I forgot to mention, Marco is vegetarian, so the plov might be a problem.

questions.prompt: Why might the guests miss the morning train?
options: Their flight now lands too late
questions.explanation: "We'll only land at seven fifteen that morning, which is far too tight for the eight o'clock train."

questions.prompt: What would Lucía prefer to drop?
questions.explanation: "If something has to go, maybe drop the bazaar."

questions.prompt: What does she say about Marco?

children.title: Send a revised plan
children.instructions: Write to Lucía with a revised plan: solve the travel-time problem, explain what you've changed in the programme, and say how you've dealt with Marco's diet.
children.prompt_text:
To: Lucía
Subject: Re: Thursday in Samarkand
children.goal: Propose a workable new plan that respects the guests' priorities.

points.label: explain the change to the programme

children.model_answer:
Dear Lucía,
Thank you for letting me know, and no problem at all. I've booked you both on the 9:30 fast train instead, and our driver will pick you up at the airport and take you straight to the station. We'll still have a full guided visit of Registan, starting at 12:15. To make up the time, we'll skip the bazaar and have a later lunch. I've spoken to the restaurant, and they will prepare a vegetarian menu for Marco. The rest of the day stays the same.
Best wishes,
Malika

children.title: Welcome the guests at Registan
children.instructions: You arrive at Registan with Lucía and Marco. Welcome them, tell them one thing about the place, and outline the rest of the day.
children.prompt_text: Lucía: Wow, so this is it! What's the plan from here?
children.goal: Give a warm, informative welcome and a clear outline of the day.

points.label: outline the rest of the day

children.model_answer: Welcome to Registan! These three madrasas were built between the fifteenth and the seventeenth centuries, and they're famous for their blue tiles. We'll spend about an hour and a half here, then have lunch, with a vegetarian menu for Marco, and after that we'll visit the Gur-e-Amir Mausoleum.
